stories.headline: Huang allies push Nvidia comeback as Bessent demands outside CEO and answers within 10 days

key_facts.fact: Jensen Huang has discussed a return as Nvidia CEO with confidants, and an ally is assembling a 'war room' of Silicon Valley executives to lobby the board and seek White House support, the Financial Times reported on Nov. 15; the ally said Huang backed the effort.
key_facts.excerpt: One ally told the paper they were putting together a "war room" of Silicon Valley executives to lobby Nvidia's board for his return and would try to win support from the White House. The ally said Huang backed the effort.

key_facts.fact: Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney backed a public 'Bring Jensen Back' letter; shareholders Brad Gerstner (Altimeter) and Gavin Baker (Atreides) urged the board to keep Huang's return on the table. Huang holds no controlling stake and cannot overrule the board.
key_facts.excerpt: Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney have backed a public letter calling on Nvidia's board to "Bring Jensen Back." ... Huang doesn't hold a controlling stake in Nvidia and can't overrule its board.

key_facts.fact: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Fox News on Nov. 15 that Nvidia needs a 'dramatic shakeup' and that the board should go outside the company for its next CEO.
key_facts.excerpt: "This makes me think that as the board conducts a search for a new leader that they need to go outside the company, that just (with) what was going on inside the company, they need a dramatic shakeup," Bessent told Fox News' "Sunday Morning Futures" show.

key_facts.fact: Bessent said the board and outside counsel must answer within 10 days questions about Nvidia's culture of export-control compliance, asking whether it pressed 'seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings'.
key_facts.excerpt: "I want to keep coming back to what was the culture at Nvidia, and were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?" Bessent said in an interview on Fox News.

key_facts.fact: Bessent questioned Nvidia's disclosures, noting it stopped reporting Singapore revenue separately in November 2025, and said: 'If this were a bank ... the OCC would be in there right now, and a lot of the executives would be removed.'
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia stopped separately reporting Singapore revenue in November 2025, saying a new methodology based on customers' headquarters rather than billing addresses better reflected the geographic distribution of its sales.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia reports quarterly results on Tuesday, Nov. 17, its first since Huang's resignation; interim CEO Colette Kress has scheduled a company-wide meeting for Wednesday, and the board said it has not hired a search firm. The FT earlier reported the board approached Arm CEO Rene Haas.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia reports quarterly earnings Tuesday, its first since Huang's resignation. Interim CEO Colette Kress has scheduled a company-wide meeting for Wednesday ... The FT reported Friday that the board had approached Arm CEO Rene Haas.

key_facts.fact: Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick are feuding over Commerce's failure to blacklist Megaspeed; both are expected to accompany Trump to China this week.
key_facts.excerpt: Both Bessent and Lutnick are expected to accompany Trump to China this week, Semafor reported Sunday.

stories.headline: Nvidia's interim CEO expected to rein in AI financing; Huang had told neoclouds to get prepayments

key_facts.fact: Interim CEO Colette Kress is expected to rein in Nvidia's financing of the AI industry, the Wall Street Journal reported on Nov. 15; Huang had already begun a pullback in his final months.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia's interim chief executive, Colette Kress, is expected to rein in its financing of the AI industry, The Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday. Jensen Huang had already started that pullback in his final months as CEO.

key_facts.fact: At Nvidia's GTC in Berlin in October, Huang told neocloud CEOs to secure upfront payments from their customers to get GPU allocations, saying 'I could just give all this capacity to Elon! Elon wants it.'
key_facts.excerpt: "You're not charging what you should be charging. I don't even need you guys. I could just give all this capacity to Elon! Elon wants it."

key_facts.fact: Nvidia took part in a record 129 venture deals over the past year (27% of global venture deal value), and its latest filing lists $36 billion of off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia took part in a record 129 venture deals over the past year ... That was 27% of global venture deal value. Nvidia's latest quarterly filing lists $36bn of off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements.

key_facts.fact: UBS analyst Tim Arcuri estimated a pullback could take $50 billion or more out of the market; founders of low-revenue startups told the Journal they could struggle to raise money without Nvidia.
key_facts.excerpt: UBS analyst Tim Arcuri estimated that a pullback could take $50bn or more out of the market.

key_facts.fact: In August Nvidia scaled back its commitment to OpenAI's Piketon, Ohio data-center lease after Kress grew skeptical; open deals include Nscale's $45 billion Anthropic data center in West Virginia and a Thinking Machines investment at a $40 billion valuation.
key_facts.excerpt: In August, Nvidia cut the scale of its commitment to OpenAI's data centre lease in Piketon, Ohio ... Nscale is negotiating with Nvidia and other investors to back a $45bn data centre for Anthropic in West Virginia.

stories.headline: Nvidia appealed to Taiwan officials over manager charged in China server-smuggling case

key_facts.fact: Nvidia expressed concerns to Taiwanese political officials about the July arrest of a manager surnamed Chang, indicted in August for forgery and breach of trust, Bloomberg reported on Nov. 15.
key_facts.excerpt: The company expressed concerns to political officials about the July arrest of an Nvidia manager surnamed Chang, who was indicted in August on charges of forgery and breach of trust.

key_facts.fact: Prosecutors call Chang the 'core figure' of a network that allegedly smuggled 74 servers with Nvidia chips to China and tried to divert 56 more, seized by Taiwan's Coast Guard in May.
key_facts.excerpt: Taiwanese prosecutors described Chang as the "core figure" of a network that allegedly smuggled 74 servers containing Nvidia chips to China before attempting to divert another 56 that were seized by Taiwan's Coast Guard in May.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia representatives told officials they disagreed with the charges; officials replied they had no role in the proceedings. Nvidia also sought advice from TSMC, which declined to get involved.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia representatives told Taiwanese officials that the company disagreed with the prosecutors' allegations against Zhang and believed he should not be under investigation ... TSMC declined to intervene.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia said its internal investigation found 'no indication that our employee knew of the alleged diversion effort by employees at other companies'. It is the first known prosecution of an Nvidia employee over chip diversion.
key_facts.excerpt: This is the first known case in which an Nvidia employee has been prosecuted over chip diversion activities.

key_facts.fact: Chang is one of nine defendants, including two Super Micro employees, and faces up to five years in prison; Nvidia has no government-relations director in Taiwan and only recently advertised the job.
key_facts.excerpt: Chang faces up to five years in prison, and the case is now before a district court. He is one of nine defendants, including two employees of Super Micro.

stories.headline: US and nine Pax Silica partners sign accord to jointly protect AI chip supply chains from China

key_facts.fact: On Nov. 15 the US and nine Pax Silica participants signed the San Francisco Declaration at the Pax Silica Founders Retreat, convened by Under Secretary of State Jacob Helberg.
key_facts.excerpt: On November 15, the United States and nine Pax Silica participants signed the San Francisco Declaration on the Secure Foundations of Enduring Prosperity at the Pax Silica Founders Retreat, convened by Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg.

key_facts.fact: Signatories alongside the US: Australia, India, Israel, Japan, South Korea, Qatar, Singapore, the UAE and the UK; Germany, Sweden, the Netherlands and the European Commission are expected to sign next week.
key_facts.excerpt: Germany, Sweden, the Netherlands and the European Commission will sign next week.

key_facts.fact: The declaration sets a common definition of sensitive technologies and critical infrastructure in 'Super Intelligence' supply chains, from chips and their means of production to ports and energy, whose theft or illicit transfer would give hostile actors a military or intelligence advantage.
key_facts.excerpt: sensitive technologies — including goods, software, materials, knowledge, components and inputs used to produce them, and their means of production essential to SI supply chains, whose theft, illicit transfer, or acquisition by hostile actors would confer a meaningful military or intelligence advantage

key_facts.fact: Participants will set up five working groups, including supply-chain cooperation across the SI stack, safe harbors and supply-chain security hubs, and SI security and resilience.
key_facts.excerpt: five proposed groups covering pro-innovation policy frameworks, SI adoption in key sectors, supply chain cooperation across the SI stack, safe harbors and supply chain security hubs, and SI security and resilience.

key_facts.fact: Helberg: 'The knowhow to design a chip, the machine that makes it and the port that ships it can all be in different countries'; the accord comes ahead of Trump's meeting with Xi at the APEC summit in Shenzhen.
key_facts.excerpt: "What makes the San Francisco Declaration historic is that Pax Silica partners have agreed to treat the security of those technologies and the infrastructure behind them as a shared responsibility."

stories.headline: SK Hynix commits $1.05B to Korean chip suppliers and details $655M shared 'Trinity Fab' test line

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix said on Nov. 16 it will spend 1.4 trillion won ($1.05 billion) over five years to support domestic suppliers of chip materials, parts and equipment, across R&D, testing, mass production and sales.
key_facts.excerpt: SK Hynix said on Monday (Nov 16) it plans to spend 1.4 trillion won (US$1.05 billion) over the next five years to support domestic suppliers of semiconductor materials, parts and equipment

key_facts.fact: Trinity Fab, an 874.6 billion won testing facility in the first fab of the Yongin cluster, is funded by SK Hynix (443.2B won), the central government (373.6B won) and local governments (57.7B won); it is scheduled to open in May 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: It is scheduled to open in May 2027. SK Hynix will contribute 443.2 billion won, the central government 373.6 billion won and local governments 57.7 billion won

key_facts.fact: The 3,305 sq m cleanroom will let smaller suppliers test lithography, etching, deposition and inspection products on 12-inch wafers under near-production conditions; it is run by an independent nonprofit foundation to protect IP.
key_facts.excerpt: It will include a 3,305 sq m cleanroom and equipment for processes including lithography, etching, deposition and inspection. Suppliers will be able to evaluate materials and equipment using 12-inch wafers

key_facts.fact: The facility sits inside the first fab of SK Hynix's Yongin cluster, 40 km south of Seoul, where the company plans to invest 600 trillion won in four fabs.
key_facts.excerpt: The facility will be housed within the first chip plant at SK Hynix's Yongin semiconductor cluster, 40km south of Seoul, where the company plans to invest 600 trillion won to build four chip fabrication plants.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix will advance up to 50% of initial development costs and pay suppliers even if projects miss targets; with financial institutions it will offer 2 trillion won in financing backed by the Korea Trade Insurance Corporation.
key_facts.excerpt: SK Hynix and financial institutions will also provide 2 trillion won in financing backed by the Korea Trade Insurance Corporation

key_facts.fact: Users of Trinity Fab have yet to be selected by an independent evaluation committee; full operations are scheduled for Q4 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The companies that will use the facility have yet to be selected. An independent evaluation committee under the foundation will review applications, with full operations scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2027.

stories.headline: Samsung pitches one-stop AI data centers; SDS in early talks to host Anthropic and OpenAI

key_facts.fact: Samsung SDS is in early-stage talks to sign Anthropic and OpenAI as tenants for its Korean AI data centers, the Financial Times reported on Nov. 15; no terms or capacity have been disclosed and none of the companies has confirmed.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung SDS is in early-stage talks with Anthropic and OpenAI to sign them as tenants for its Korean AI data centres, the Financial Times reported on 15 November.

key_facts.fact: Samsung wants to be a 'one-stop shop' that builds, runs and powers data centers: Samsung C&T builds sites and power plants, SDS designs and operates, SDI supplies batteries, Samsung Electronics chips and cooling, Samsung Heavy Industries floating data centers.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the plan Samsung C&T builds, Samsung SDS designs and operates, Samsung SDI supplies batteries, Samsung Electronics supplies chips and cooling, and Samsung Heavy Industries handles floating data centers.

key_facts.fact: Samsung SDS broke ground on Nov. 2 on an AI-only site in Gumi with 60 MW of initial capacity, expandable to 120 MW, due to start operating in March 2029.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung SDS broke ground on an AI-only site in Gumi on 2 November with "60 megawatts of initial capacity, expandable to 120 megawatts", scheduled to begin operations in March 2029.

key_facts.fact: A cited forecast of 6.6 trillion won in Samsung SDS data-center revenue by 2031 is a brokerage (iM Securities) estimate, not a company target.
key_facts.excerpt: The forecast of 6.6 trillion won in data center revenue by 2031 is a brokerage estimate, not a company target

stories.headline: Indian chip startup Bharat Semi raises $24M seed for AI image sensors, wins General Atomics design

key_facts.fact: New Delhi-based Bharat Semi raised a $24 million all-equity seed round led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons and Indus Bridge Ventures, with Micromax, Valour Capital and Gaingels participating.
key_facts.excerpt: The all-equity seed round was led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons, and Indus Bridge Ventures, with participation from Valour Capital, Micromax, Gaingels, and individual investors.

key_facts.fact: It develops programmable image sensors combining capture, processing and AI on one chip, which co-founder Vrinda Kapoor says could cut system costs by at least 70% versus separate sensor, ISP and SoC.
key_facts.excerpt: The move could cut system costs by at least 70% compared with conventional setups that use a separate image sensor, image signal processor, and a system-on-chip

key_facts.fact: The pre-revenue startup has design wins with US defense firm General Atomics and India's Kaynes Semicon, and targets initial commercial production in 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: it has secured design wins with U.S. defense technology company General Atomics and India's Kaynes Semicon ... targeting its initial commercial production in 2027.

key_facts.fact: Bharat Semi initially targeted $10-15 million but raised its goal to about $25 million on investor demand; it was valued at $149 million post-money in January 2026, per Tracxn.
key_facts.excerpt: Bharat Semi initially targeted a seed round of $10-15 million but raised its target to around $25 million following strong investor interest.
